afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 122148
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
248 PM MST Mon Oct 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Periods of isolated to scattered showers will continue today
  through Tuesday morning.
  
- Temperatures will continue to cool through the first half of the
  week with highs dipping into the seventies, while overnight 
  lows easily reach into the fifties for Tuesday and Wednesday. 

- Dry weather will settle in by Wednesday before breezy to windy
  conditions return later in the week and temperatures slowly 
  return to near normal.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

The local area remains downstream of a large Western CONUS trough 
and under a persistent strong SSW flow. Isolated to scattered 
showers continue to develop across portions of south-central AZ. 
Mesoanalysis shows this is a high shear - low CAPE environment and 
with warm southerly flow and a lot of dry air aloft, above 700mb, 
there has hardly been any lightning with the activity so far today. 
Regardless, the showers have been strong enough at times to produce 
high rain-rates, with some instantaneous rates observed up to 1-
2"/hr. Unfortunately the showers are zoomin', moving NE at roughly 
30 kts (35 mph). This has inhibited the potential of receiving any 
significant rainfall from any one shower. However, with the 
uniform shear, several showers have formed into linear segments or
have developed along convergent cloud streets and this allowed 
for a few areas to pick up a quick 0.25-0.50". Shower chances are 
expected to continue through this afternoon and evening, but they 
will may become more isolated across the lower deserts and 
focused mostly over the AZ high terrain to the north, as model 
soundings show LCLs lifting (decreasing the cloud depth) and dry 
air continuing to slowly filter in.

Heading into tonight a shortwave trough at the base of the larger 
Western CONUS trough is expected to swing through the area with a 
weak surface frontal boundary. PoPs go up again in response to this, 
up to 40-70% between 10 PM and 5 PM - with the latest NBM - 
across Maricopa and Pinal Counties. Showers should then shift 
completely east of the Phoenix area by the afternoon tomorrow as 
even more dry air filters in aloft. Despite the shortwave and 
front, rainfall is expected to remain on the light side, 
especially with showers still moving very fast. Most areas are 
likely to receive less than 0.25" (this includes receiving nothing
at all), with latest HREF only showing around a 10% chance of 
receiving >0.25" across the lower deserts with tonight's activity.
Highest rainfall potential will be across the higher terrain 
areas east and northeast of Phoenix. A few isolated spots of up to
1" or more will still be possible where stronger showers train 
over the same area.

A much stronger cold front will sweep through the area tomorrow 
night through Wednesday morning as the deep low pressure at the 
center of the large Western CONUS trough digs through the northern 
half of AZ. This will be a dry front that will clean out much of the 
lingering low level moisture. Dew point temperatures are forecast to 
go from the mid to upper 50s Tuesday afternoon in the Phoenix area 
to dipping below 50 degrees by Wednesday afternoon. Mean mixing 
ratios will also drop to 3-5 g/kg across the area by Wednesday 
afternoon. So, no additional showers are expected heading into 
Wednesday as the dry air surges in. In addition to the drying 
conditions midweek, the low Wednesday will lead to the development 
of a N-S pressure gradient leading to increasing northerly winds 
across southeast California and far western Arizona early Wednesday 
likely peaking late Wednesday morning before the gradient relaxes. 
Wind gusts of 25-30 mph can be expected across much of the Lower CO 
River Valley Wednesday morning into the afternoon. 

Temperatures today will not get much warmer than they currently are 
early this afternoon. Most lower deserts are in the 70s to low-80s. 
With the shortwave trough tonight and then stronger upper low moving 
through tomorrow night, the next couple days are forecast to be 
cooler. The latest NBM forecast has just about all lower desert 
locations failing to reach 80 degrees tomorrow and again for 
Wednesday across south-central AZ. Perhaps more notable will be the 
much cooler low temperatures. Morning low temperatures will be 
dipping into the 50s across the lower deserts; coolest on Wednesday. 
Some areas will even dip into the 40s, like up around Wickenburg, 
and portions of Joshua Tree NP will fall into the 30s. This will be 
the coldest push of air since the Spring. The last time Phoenix Sky 
Harbor reported a low below 60 degrees was March 11. Don't let the 
snowbirds know!

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...  

Models are finally coming into better agreement for late this week 
into the weekend showing shortwave energy and an upper level jet max 
diving southwestward through the region on Thursday. At the same 
time a strong upper level ridge just off the West Coast will move 
inland. For now, it seems this set up will result in a weak cut-off 
low forming somewhere to our southwest by Friday with ridging 
settling in just to our north. To complicate things even more, a 
polar air mass will quickly dive through the Plains States Thursday 
potentially bringing a back-door cool front into eastern Arizona 
Friday morning. Even though this is a complex pattern, it really 
won't amount to much for our area as dry air will remain entrenched 
enough to keep rain chances below 10%. 

However, it is looking increasingly likely a strong pressure 
gradient will develop across Arizona by Friday leading to breezy to 
locally windy easterly winds developing Thursday night into Friday 
morning. NBM guidance does show the potential for Advisory level 
winds, but from past experience these winds tend to be overdone. We 
should at least expect occasional wind gusts of 25-35 mph to maybe 
some 35-40 mph possible across far southern Gila County, Pinal 
County, into southern Maricopa County. These gusty easterly winds 
will be more pronounced during the latter half of the morning before 
diminishing some during the afternoon. Guidance suggests a repeat of 
these gusty winds on Saturday before the gradient begins to relax 
into Sunday. Moderating temperatures are forecast for late week with 
highs warming into the 80s by Thursday and likely staying at or just 
below normal through next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1755Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

Gusty winds, periods of VFR CIGs between 5-7K ft AGL, and periods
of VCSH/SHRA will be the main aviation weather concerns through
Tuesday afternoon. While confidence is not high, the best timing for
VCSH/SHRA will be now through approximately 21Z this afternoon 
and late tonight into early Tuesday morning. Better coverage is 
expected with the latter period of SHRA, and so have included 
PROB30 direct impacts at the terminals (lowered CIGS, still likely
in the VFR category, and briefly lowered VIS, likely dipping into
a MVFR range). After a couple hours with a prevailing S'rly
cross-runway component at KPHX and KDVT, winds will shift
predominantly out of SSW'rly to W'rly directions, however, 
a period of VRB or light SE will be possible overnight into early
Tuesday morning. Gusts through the afternoon will peak between 
20-25 kts and are then expected to subside early this evening. VFR
CIGs will begin to clear the airspace late Tuesday morning into 
the afternoon. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

Gusty winds will be the main aviation weather issue through the
TAF period under FEW-SCT and at times BKN midlevel cloud decks. 
Winds will favor W at KIPL and SW at KBLH through the TAF period.
Winds have already increased at KIPL with gusts as high as the low
30s, and gusts are expected to develop and peak this afternoon at
KBLH around 25 kts. Gusts will then begin to subside after 
sunset at KBLH and late this evening at KIPL.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Periods of isolated to scattered showers are expected through 
tonight before a weak cold front moves through and drier air
begins to filter in tomorrow. A stronger and drier front will
follow tomorrow night into Wednesday. Elevated moisture levels 
will keep MinRHs mostly above 40% through tomorrow before 
lowering down to 20-35% Wednesday and Thursday. Breezy conditions 
are expected just about every day. A northerly gradient wind will 
develop across southeast CA and southwest AZ tomorrow and 
strengthen each day through the middle of the week, with morning 
and afternoon gusts up to 20-30 mph. Stronger breezes will spread 
to the rest of AZ by Friday with breezy to windy easterlies 
developing. Below normal temperatures are expected through at 
least the middle of the week. Moisture return late week into the 
weekend may bring a return of rain chances.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Whittock 
FIRE WEATHER...Benedict/Kuhlman
